Favvy, as it would come off the printer

This is the actual 3D model, shown in printed plastic with the fine layer lines a real print has, sitting on a counter next to an iPhone for scale. Drag to turn it, pinch or scroll to zoom. The QR code is real: it opens the FavCircles App Clip (api.favcircles.com/s/JOINUS here). Each store's figure gets its own code.

Built to take a knock

  • One solid piece. The heart, arms, feet and base print together as a single solid part. Nothing is glued on, so nothing can snap off or come loose.
  • Sits right on the base. The bottom of the heart is printed into the base, and the feet are half sunk into it on either side. That makes a wide, solid joint instead of a point.
  • Short, thick arms. About 1.6 cm thick and rooted deep inside the body. There are no thin parts sticking out to catch on a bag or a sleeve.
  • Heavy and grippy. A steel washer hidden in the base adds weight so it won't tip, and four stick-on rubber bumpers stop it sliding when someone taps it.
  • NFC tag sealed inside. A 25 mm NFC sticker sits under the QR code, completely enclosed in plastic. It can't be peeled off or picked at.

How it's made

  1. Program the NFC tag with the store's link and test it with a phone.
  2. Start the print: the whole figure, upright, in 4 colors on a Bambu printer with an AMS (or similar). The arms are angled so no supports are needed.
  3. The printer pauses before the 5.00 mm layer, when the pocket is still open. Stick the NFC tag into its pocket and resume; the QR code prints over it.
  4. When it's done, glue a 32 mm steel washer into the recess underneath and stick on the four rubber bumpers. Test a tap and a scan.

Four colors: pink, deep pink, white and black. That's one standard 4-slot AMS, so any store's figure can be printed on the same setup. Printed solid (high infill) in PETG or PLA.

Printing it on your Bambu P1S with AMS

  1. Load the AMS: slot 1 pink, slot 2 a deeper pink or magenta, slot 3 white, slot 4 black. Bambu PLA Basic or PLA Matte works well (matte hides layer lines).
  2. Open Bambu Studio and drag in all four files from the store's folder, favvy-print/bambu/<code>/, at once. Make a store's folder with ./make-figure.sh <code>: the register code to earn points, or the window code to save the store. When it asks "Load these files as a single object with multiple parts?", choose Yes. They snap together into one figure.
  3. Set colors: in the object list, give each part its slot: favvy-pink → 1, favvy-deep → 2, favvy-white → 3, favvy-black → 4.
  4. Settings: 0.16 mm layers (the "Fine" profile), 4 walls, 30–40% gyroid infill, no supports. Turn on "Flush into objects' infill" to waste less filament on color changes.
  5. Add the NFC pause: after slicing, drag the layer slider on the right to 5.00 mm, the first layer that covers the round pocket (with the 0.16 mm Fine profile). The layer below, 4.84 mm, should still show the pocket open. Right-click and choose Add pause; the printer stops before printing that layer.
  6. Print. When it pauses, peel the programmed NFC sticker (25 mm round NTAG213 or NTAG215, written with the same App Clip link and locked) and stick it flat on the floor of the round pocket under the QR area, then resume. Bambu Studio puts it at about 13 hours in two colors (more in four), and a one-color test at about 2 hours. Most of the extra time is filament swaps, because the face and QR code run through hundreds of layers.
  7. Finish: glue a 32 mm (1¼ in) steel fender washer into the recess underneath (it slides in after printing) and stick four 10 mm rubber bumpers under the base so it doesn't slide.

The color changes add filament waste (purge) and time. That's normal for AMS prints. A test print first is worth it: check the QR scans with a phone and the tag reads through the plastic.
